name: Hashabiah
overview: Hashabiah was a male Levite known as the son of Jeduthun and a descendant of Hebron. He was set apart to prophesy musically with lyres, harps, and cymbals, serving as one of the chosen singers in the temple worship. Notably, he was the twelfth chosen by lot among the singers, highlighting his special role in the Levitical musical ministry.
namesAndTitles: The name Hashabiah means 'YHWH has reckoned,' reflecting a divine acknowledgment or appointment. This proper name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 25:3 and reveals a connection to God's sovereign plan, though it was not specifically given by God.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Hashabiah as the son of Jeduthun, explicitly noted in 1 Chronicles 25:3, and he is linked to the lineage of Merari as a descendant according to 1 Chronicles 9:14. Additionally, Azrikam is inferred as his father in 1 Chronicles 9:14, and Bunni is mentioned as another son in Nehemiah 11:14, situating Hashabiah within a notable Levitical family.
scriptureSignificance: Hashabiah's significance lies in his role within the Levitical singers who were divinely appointed to prophesy through music during temple worship. Being the twelfth chosen by lot among the singers emphasizes the order and divine selection in the ministry of music and prophecy. His descent from Jeduthun and Hebron connects him to a respected lineage responsible for maintaining sacred worship practices, underscoring the importance of musical prophecy in Israel's spiritual life.
